title: Distributed Persistence Domain for Persistent Memory Pooling
event_hint: Proposes moving persistence support into the CXL switch (Persistent CXL Switch + Distributed Persistence Domain abstraction), cutting persist latency ~33% over volatile CXL switches while preserving crash consistency.
problem: CXL enables memory pooling over disaggregated memory and can improve utilization for persistent memory systems, but integrating persistence semantics into CXL-based pooling introduces substantial latency that limits scalability, because persist operations must traverse the entire CXL fabric (switches, links, protocol layers). Centralized persistence-domain correctness assumptions break if persistence is moved into the network.
mechanism: Proposes Distributed Persistence Domain (DPD), a new abstraction for persistent memory pooling that enables persistence support at the CXL switch level. The paper formalizes the distributed persistence domain, uses DPD as a framework to identify correctness hazards when persistence structures are distributed across the fabric, and derives design requirements to guarantee correctness. The proposed Persistent CXL Switch incorporates persistence support to reduce persist latency, enable read forwarding, and coalesce writes while preserving correctness and crash consistency.

evidence.claim: Persistent CXL Switch achieves an average speedup of 33% over volatile CXL switches across SPLASH-4 and YCSB benchmarks.
Up to 36% speedup with the read-forwarding optimization across all workloads.
evidence.condition: with read forwarding; SPLASH-4 and YCSB

evidence.claim: Persist latency overhead arises because persist operations must traverse the entire CXL fabric including switches, links, and protocol layers.
Moving persistence support into the network breaks the traditional correctness assumptions of centralized persistence domains; DPD formalizes hazards and derives correctness requirements.

evaluation_context: Simulation-based evaluation; benchmarks SPLASH-4 and YCSB; baseline is volatile (standard) CXL switches; metrics include speedup and persist latency.
limitations: Simulation-based (no silicon/real-CXL-switch hardware); abstract-level, detailed breakdown of crash-consistency protocol and failure modes requires full text. Workloads limited to SPLASH-4 and YCSB. Full body not fetched.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to CXL/disaggregated memory: it tackles the persist-latency bottleneck in CXL persistent-memory pooling and proposes a switch-level offload design (analogous in spirit to SmartNIC/DPU offload but for the CXL fabric), with concrete speedups. Relevant to memory-DSA and pooled-memory roadmaps where persistence + disaggregation intersect.
